head: Neutrophil granulopoiesis
name: Neutrophil granulopoiesis (G-CSF/GM-CSF signaling, transcriptional control, negative regulation)
rationale: All members drive or restrain neutrophil production from myeloid progenitors; the CSF signaling and negative-regulation members separate it from progenitor, monocyte-macrophage and eosinophil/mast cell themes.

head: Global-genome excision repair of UV damage
name: Global-genome excision repair of UV damage (lesion recognition, dual incision)
rationale: Members cover UV pyrimidine dimer recognition and incision by global-genome NER, distinct from gap-filling/translesion synthesis themes and from transcription-coupled NER.

head: Beta-catenin-TCF transcription and its repression
name: Beta-catenin-TCF transcription and its repression (AXIN/APC mutants, RUNX3)
rationale: Members concern the nuclear beta-catenin-TCF output of canonical Wnt and its negative control, unlike confusables centred on receptor, DVL and ligand-level Wnt events.

head: Pentose metabolism
name: Pentose metabolism (non-oxidative pentose phosphate branch, glucuronate-xylulose pathway, xylulose 5-phosphate)
rationale: Members interconvert pentose phosphates via the non-oxidative shunt and the glucuronate-xylulose route, separating them from fructose, polyol and galactose themes.

head: Receptor tyrosine kinase-driven AKT/ERK activation
name: Receptor tyrosine kinase-driven AKT/ERK activation (oncogenic fusions and amplifications, FGFR/PDGFR/ALK/LTK)
rationale: Members are RTKs, mostly oncogenic fusion and amplification variants, signaling to PI3K-AKT and ERK, distinct from normal ERBB/MET/FGFR cascades and TKI-resistance mutant themes.

head: Apical membrane trafficking in ductal epithelia
name: Apical membrane trafficking in ductal epithelia (CFTR anion-water secretion, membrane rafts, pancreatic duct)
rationale: Members build and use the polarized surface of secretory ductal epithelia for CFTR-driven fluid secretion, unlike confusables on ion channels, tight junctions or lipid flippases.

head: HGF-MET and TGF-beta/activin receptor signaling
name: HGF-MET and TGF-beta/activin receptor signaling (cancer mutants, TGFBR3 co-receptor, AMH receptor)
rationale: Members split between HGF-MET (and MSP) receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and TGF-beta/activin/AMH receptor-SMAD signaling with cancer mutants, with no single shared process; the TGF-beta half separates it from PTK6, liver and RTK confusables.

head: Monocyte-macrophage differentiation
name: Monocyte-macrophage differentiation (M-CSF signaling, macrophage proliferation, myeloid dendritic cells)
rationale: Members promote M-CSF-driven monocyte, macrophage and myeloid dendritic cell development, unlike the granulocyte and interleukin-signaling confusables.

head: MITF-M-dependent gene regulation
name: MITF-M-dependent gene regulation (non-pigmentation targets, invasion and proliferation, lysosome and metabolism)
rationale: Members are MITF-M control and its target programmes outside pigmentation, which separates the theme from melanin and pigmentation confusables.

head: RNA polymerase II elongation control
name: RNA polymerase II elongation control (promoter escape, pausing, termination)
rationale: Most members govern Pol II passage from promoter clearance through pausing, elongation and termination (two translation-elongation terms are minor outliers), unlike broader RNA processing and Pol I/III confusables.

head: Nutrient-sensing transcriptional control of metabolism
name: Nutrient-sensing transcriptional control of metabolism (lipogenesis and gluconeogenesis, ChREBP/SREBP/LXR, circadian clock)
rationale: Members are sugar-, lipid- and energy-sensing transcriptional regulators of lipid and glucose metabolism, distinct from adipogenesis, glucagon-PKA and cholesterol-SREBP confusables.

head: Mitochondrial protein import
name: Mitochondrial protein import (outer membrane, matrix)
rationale: Members deliver proteins across the outer membrane into the matrix, unlike confusables on mitochondrial protein processing, degradation or respiratory complex assembly.

head: Death receptor-induced extrinsic apoptosis
name: Death receptor-induced extrinsic apoptosis (Fas and TRAIL, caspase-8 and c-FLIP, BID)
rationale: Members form the Fas/TRAIL to caspase-8 apoptotic route and its c-FLIP control, separate from necroptosis and intrinsic mitochondrial apoptosis confusables.

head: Rho subfamily GTPase cycle
name: Rho subfamily GTPase cycle (RhoA, RhoB, RhoC)
rationale: Members are the GTPase cycles of the three Rho subfamily members, distinct from Rac, Cdc42 and atypical Rho confusables.

head: Stress and innate motivated behavior
name: Stress and innate motivated behavior (glucocorticoid-CRH response, fear, reproductive and aggressive behavior)
rationale: Members are innate behaviors and behavioral stress responses (mating, parenting, aggression, drinking, fear, CRH/corticosterone), unlike confusables on neuropeptide signaling, HPA secretion, sleep or drug reward.

head: Endocrine hormone synthesis and signaling
name: Endocrine hormone synthesis and signaling (adrenal-gonadal steroidogenesis, thyroid hormone, GH-prolactin-leptin)
rationale: Members make or respond to classical endocrine hormones, distinguishing the theme from vitamin A/D/K and phosphate-mineral confusables and from GH-secretion/amino-acid transport.

head: Branched-chain amino acid catabolism
name: Branched-chain amino acid catabolism (leucine, valine, organic acidurias)
rationale: Members are leucine and valine breakdown steps and their inborn errors, unlike confusables featuring isoleucine, biotin or short-chain fatty acid metabolism.

head: Proteotoxic stress response
name: Proteotoxic stress response (HSF1 heat shock, stress granules, mitochondrial UPR)
rationale: Members respond to protein-damaging stress via HSF1 refolding, stress granules and UPRmt, unlike confusables on chaperonin folding, the ER UPR or aggrephagy.

head: RIG-I-like receptor antiviral signaling
name: RIG-I-like receptor antiviral signaling (feedback regulation, NF-kB and IRF3 output, dsRNA sensing)
rationale: Members are cytosolic RNA sensing by RIG-I/MDA5 and its positive and negative regulation, distinct from TLR, cGAS-STING and broader interferon response confusables.

head: Triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism
name: Triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism (chylomicron and VLDL assembly, lipolysis, clearance)
rationale: Members cover dietary fat absorption and the assembly, lipase remodeling and clearance of chylomicrons and VLDL, unlike LDL/HDL remodeling and phospholipase confusables.

head: TCA cycle and 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases
name: TCA cycle and 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases (protein lipoylation, Fe-S cluster assembly, lysine/glycine catabolism)
rationale: Members are TCA reactions and the lipoylated, Fe-S-dependent enzymes that feed and run them, distinct from CoA/PDH regulation and serine/vitamin B6 confusables.

head: Epithelial hexose transport
name: Epithelial hexose transport (intestinal absorption, renal glucose reabsorption, SGLT/GLUT defects)
rationale: Members move glucose, galactose and fructose across gut and kidney epithelia and their inherited defects, unlike carbohydrate digestion, galactose catabolism, urate and amino acid transport confusables.

head: Canonical NF-kappaB activation via RIP1
name: Canonical NF-kappaB activation via RIP1 (TNFR1 signaling, linear ubiquitination, TLR4-TRIF)
rationale: Members are RIP1-dependent IKK recruitment downstream of TNFR1 and TLR4, separating the theme from non-canonical NF-kB, IRAK-dependent TLR and negative-regulation confusables.

head: Lysosomal glycosphingolipid catabolism
name: Lysosomal glycosphingolipid catabolism (gangliosidoses, sialidosis, glycolipid transport)
rationale: Members degrade and move glycosphingolipids through the lysosome, unlike glycosphingolipid biosynthesis and sialic acid/N-glycan confusables.

head: Ras-ERK signal regulation
name: Ras-ERK signal regulation (phosphatase attenuation, RSK activation, p38 via RIT/RIN)
rationale: Members tune Ras-MAPK signaling up and down and carry its RSK and p38 outputs, distinct from confusables on RAF activation, RAS mutants and GAP-mediated control.
